title: Fear
text:
The shadow of a doubt rises over me

when the lull of your voice reaches my ear;

fear of knowing you; but in the fear there is so much

passion that it seems to me I have known you already.


I guessed the singing mystery of your throat.

Could it be that I dreamed it? Perhaps I sensed it:

woman when she promises and nest when she sings;

lie in the promise and abandonment in the nest.


Perhaps not knowing each other would be better; I feel

near you the assault of a bad presentiment

that puts a cowardly emotion on my lips.


And if the thirst to know you appears in my eyes,

my boldnesses go toward you, strange and strong woman,

but love shouts at me: if you have arrived too late!...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's tension between desire, foreboding, and the warning of lateness.

title: No Foreign Sky Protected Me...
text:
No foreign sky protected me,

no strange wing shielded my face,

I stood as witness to a common destiny,

survivor of that time, of that place.




1961
editorial_note: The translation preserves the compact witness statement and the source date.

title: No, It Is Not Mine: It Is Another People's Wound
text:
No, it is not mine: it is another people's wound.

I would never have endured it. Therefore,

take away all that happened, hide it, bury it.

Remove the lamps...

Night.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's refusal of ownership and abrupt extinguishing into night.

title: Epigram
text:
Could Beatrice have written like Dante,

or Laura glorified the pains of love?

I establish the style for woman's word.

God help me silence them again!




1960
editorial_note: The translation keeps the literary reversal from muse to maker and the source date.

title: Fragment
text:
It seemed to me that the flames of your eyes

would fly with me until dawn.

I could not understand the color

of your strange eyes.

Everything around was pulsing.

I never knew whether you were my enemy or my friend,

or whether now it was winter or summer.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the fragment's disorientation around eyes, allegiance, and season.

title: Three Things Delighted Him
text:
Three things delighted him:

white peacocks, evening prayers

and faded maps of America.

He could not stand shrieking brats,

nor raspberry jam with his tea,

nor female hysteria

...and he was bound to me.




1911
editorial_note: The translation keeps the clipped list of tastes and aversions before the final attachment.

title: The Weeks Escape from the Mind
text:
The weeks escape the mind,

I doubt it happened:

how inside your prison, little one,

the white nights froze in flames:

and still, while I catch my breath,

they set their vulture eyes

on what the great cross shows them:

this body of your death.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the broken recollection of prison, white nights, and the exposed body of death.

title: Some Go by a Straight Path
text:
Some go by a straight path,

others walk in circles,

they long for the return to the father's house

and wait for the friend of other times.

My road, instead, is neither straight nor curved,

I carry misfortune with me,

I go toward never, toward nowhere,

like a train over the abyss.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the contrast between ordinary paths and the speaker's abyss-bound route.

title: Peacefully Flows the Quiet Don
text:
Peacefully flows the Quiet Don;

to my house seeps the yellow moon.

It hops over the windowsill with its cap askew

and stops in the shadow, that yellow moon.

This woman is sick to the marrow,

this woman is completely alone,

with her husband dead, and her son distant

in prison. Pray for me. Pray.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the moon's strange entrance and the plain plea from isolation.

title: When You Hear the Thunder You Will Remember Me
text:
When you hear the thunder you will remember me

and perhaps think I loved the storm...

The streaking of the sky will look fiercely crimson

and the heart, as then, will be on fire.


This will happen one day in Moscow

when I leave the city forever

and rush toward the desired port

leaving among you barely my shadow.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the remembered storm and the speaker's departure as little more than shadow.
